title: PHP-FPM persistent connections permit request smuggling and code execution
summary: Unread request-body bytes can be accepted as a new FastCGI request on a reused connection. Forged parameters can bypass front-end routing and execute PHP as the worker.

severity.rationale: Remote code execution needs persistent backend connections and a specific unread-input path. These preconditions prevent treating every PHP installation as exposed.

exposure: The application must open php://input without fully consuming it, the front end must reuse backend connections, and the attacker must know an existing script path. Front ends closing each FastCGI connection avoid the demonstrated attack. LSAPI shares the cleanup issue without established code execution.

params.instructions: Check PHP-FPM version, affected release line and the documented exposure conditions.

remediation.action: Update or contain the affected component
remediation.details: Upgrade to 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28 or 8.5.13 on the corresponding line.
remediation.risk: Medium. Updates can interrupt workflows and require compatibility checks.

verification: Confirm the deployed release meets the corresponding fixed version and verify the affected workflow with harmless test inputs.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.
